response:Write a concise systems analysis of dynamic batching for autoregressive language-model inference. Cover the distinction between prompt processing and token-by-token decoding, why heterogeneous prompt lengths create padding overhead, why a large batch is not automatically the best batch, how a deadline bounds queueing delay, and how a Pareto frontier can be used to select a production policy. Do not assume streaming or claim time to first token is available.

response:A team is building a reproducible benchmark of two interchangeable inference schedulers. The baseline serializes generation even when HTTP clients are concurrent. The optimized scheduler creates bounded batches using a maximum size, maximum wait, and prompt-length buckets. Propose a fair experimental method that keeps the model, generation settings, workload corpus, hardware, warm-up, and trial count constant. Explain how to report throughput, generated tokens per second, p50, p95, p99, queue time, inference time, padding overhead, and failure rate without overstating conclusions.
response:Name one benefit of dynamic batching.
response:Explain tail latency in one sentence.
response:What is inference throughput?
response:Define backpressure.
response:An inference server receives requests at uneven intervals. Explain why waiting a few milliseconds before dispatch can increase accelerator utilization while also increasing queue latency.
response:Compare sequential text generation with bounded dynamic batching. Focus on throughput, end-to-end latency, memory use, and overload behavior.
response:Describe how padding affects a decoder-only transformer batch when prompt lengths vary, and give one simple scheduling policy that reduces wasted computation.
response:A service has a fixed-size request queue and a strict request deadline. Explain what should happen when the queue is full and when a queued request reaches its deadline.
response:What is inference throughput?

response:You are reviewing the design of a small language-model inference gateway. Requests arrive concurrently, but each contains a prompt with a different token length. The gateway can either execute one request at a time or wait briefly to combine compatible requests. Discuss how batch size, wait deadline, prompt-length distribution, padding, model compute, and arrival rate jointly affect requests per second and p95 latency. End with a concrete recommendation for an interactive workload.

response:Consider an overloaded text-generation API running a causal language model on a single device. It uses an asynchronous bounded queue, groups prompts into length buckets, and dispatches when a bucket is full or its oldest item has waited too long. Explain the invariants needed to ensure that every response is correlated with the correct caller, cancellation does not leak work, errors are visible, and no request silently disappears. Include the metrics you would inspect during a load test.
